Description: The Farm to Table play kitchen is designed for pretend play and is intended for children 3 years or older. The play kitchen is primarily black and light gray with wood-like countertops and measures about 44 inches (length) x 13 ¾ inches (width) x 43 inches (height). The model number 53411 is on a sticker on the back of the play kitchen.
Title: Backyard Kids Recalls KidKraft Farm to Table Play Kitchens Due to Strangulation Hazard; One Death Reported
ConsumerContact: Contact Backyard Kids toll-free at 800-882-0234 from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET, Monday through Friday, email at recall@kidkraft.com or online at www.kidkraft.com/pages/recall for more information.

Products.Name: KidKraft Farm to Table Model Play Kitchen
Products.NumberOfUnits: About 192,000 (In addition, 12 were sold in Canada)

Images.Caption: Recalled KidKraft Farm to Table Play Kitchen
Recalled KidKraft Farm to Table Play Kitchen (the hooks are circled)

Injuries.Name: In February 2023 in Oregon, a 23-month-old child was asphyxiated after his shirt got caught on one of the hooks while climbing and crawling through the opening at the back of the play kitchen where the toy kitchen accessories are held. The child was unable to rescue himself and died from strangulation and asphyxia.

Retailers.Name: The play kitchens were sold online at KidKraft.com, Amazon.com and Walmart.com from 2018 through July 2025 for between $120 and $270.

Distributors.Name: Backyard Kids, LLC, of Plano, Texas

Hazards.Name: If young children are climbing on the counter or crawling through the opening at the back of the play kitchen, their clothing can get caught on the plastic or metal hooks meant to hold toy kitchen accessories such as play pots and pans, posing a strangulation hazard.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using the play kitchens, remove the original hooks, and contact Backyard Kids for free replacement hooks. Backyard Kids has agreed to a provide free replacement hooks to all consumers with affected units as a part of this recall.

Injuries.Name: Triangle Tube has received two reports of death due to CO poisoning associated with the recalled boilers. In 2015, a 47-year-old woman died from CO poisoning associated with a Prestige Solo 175 boiler, and in 2016, an 85-year-old man died from CO poisoning associated with a Prestige SOLO TriMax 175 boiler, following a repair. Triangle Tube has also received 25 reports of CO leaks from the recalled boilers.

Retailers.Name: The boilers were manufactured by Burnsen SA, of Belgium, from December 2011 through April 2019 and were sold by wholesale distributors and installed by independent contractors nationwide for between $3,400 and $9,700.

Importers.Name: Triangle Tube/Phase III Co. Inc., of West Deptford, New Jersey

Hazards.Name: The boilers can release carbon monoxide (CO) due to delayed ignitions or component damage, posing a risk of serious injury or death.

Remedies.Name: Consumers with recalled boilers should immediately contact Triangle Tube to schedule a free boiler inspection and, if applicable, free installation of a new boiler ignition system. Consumers who continue using the recalled boilers while awaiting repair should have working carbon monoxide alarms on each level of their homes and outside sleeping areas. Consumers who do not have a carbon monoxide alarm can contact Triangle Tube to have one shipped to them free of charge.

Description: This recall involves "GSI electronic 50W indoor pet heating comfort pad mats" with model number GKC2G002. The mats are polyester, were sold in various shapes and sizes and have a white electrical cord. They were sold in a variety of colors, including beige and pink.
Title: Heated Mats for Pets Recalled by World Class Due to Fire and Electrical Shock Hazards to Consumers; Sold Exclusively at Amazon.com
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact World Class Inc. toll-free at (888) 941-5079 between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m ET Monday through Thursday, or email the firm at gsiamazon@gmail.com

Products.Name: Indoor Pet Heating Comfort Pad Mats

Retailers.Name: Online at www.amazon.com from July 2011 through March 2012 for about $19.

Importers.Name: World Class Inc., of Brooklyn, N.Y.

Hazards.Name: The heated mats have poor wiring and construction, posing a fire and electrical shock hazard to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumer should immediately stop using the recalled pet mats and contact World Class to receive a full refund. The firm is directly contacting consumers who purchased the recalled product.

Description: The recalled product is a Ci Sport three-piece, expandable, insulated lunch box set, which includes the lunch box, aluminum bottle and the freezer gel pack. The lunch box of the recalled set has the code "1-61731-99-57" printed on one of the two white labels that are sewn under the white fastener inside the main compartment. The lunch box is 8 inches wide, 5 inches deep and 10.25 inches high. It is made of vinyl, polyester nylon and crushed nylon and has a logo with the words "Ci Sport" attached to the upper left corner. The lunch box has a carrying handle on the top and a mesh carrying pouch for the aluminum bottle on the side. The aluminum bottle measures 2.75 inches in diameter and 7.5 inches tall. The gel pack is a 6-inch by 4-inch transparent plastic pouch filled with blue liquid gel. The words "Cryofreeze" and "Ice Pack/Hot Pack" are printed in white letters on the front of the pouch. The lunch box was available in four colors: navy blue, red, black and denim blue.
Title: Expandable Lunch Boxes Recalled by California Innovations Due to Freezer Gel Pack Ingestion Hazard
ConsumerContact: For additional information, call California Innovations at (800) 722-2545 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday, e-mail ci-recall@ca-innovations.com or visit the firm's website at www.californiainnovations.com

Products.Name: Expandable Insulated Lunch Box with Freezer Gel Pack

Images.Caption: Ci Sport Expandable, Insulated Lunch Box Set

Injuries.Name: The firm has received two separate reports of a dog chewing and ingesting gel from the gel pack. One dog reportedly died from ingestion of the gel. The other was reported to have received treatment and has recovered.

Retailers.Name: Costco Wholesale Clubs, Leon Korol and Cost U Less stores between May 2007 and September 2008 for about $10.

Importers.Name: California Innovations Inc., of Toronto, Canada

Hazards.Name: Gel that contains diethylene glycol and ethylene glycol can leak out of damaged freezer gel packs, posing a poisoning hazard if ingested by children or adults.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using the gel packs and dispose of them according to federal, state and/or local regulations. It is recommended that consumers contact their local waste disposal authority for instructions. Consumers may return the lunch box set to Costco for a full refund or may receive a $5 cash refund for the gel pack only by contacting California Innovations.

Title: Costway Recalls Convertible High Chairs Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Entrapment and Fall Hazards; Violate Mandatory Standard for High Chairs
ConsumerContact: Costway toll-free at 844-242-1885 from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. PT Monday through Friday, email at recall@costway.com, or online at or www.costway.com and click on “Recall” at the bottom of the page for more information.

Hazards.Name: The convertible high chairs violate the mandatory safety standard for high chairs because they do not contain a passive restraint system and a child can slip through the opening between the feeding tray and seat and become entrapped or fall, posing a risk of serious injury or death.

Description: The Ponytail vacuums were sold under the following names: Genesis Prolux S/R Genesis LX Prolux Warehouse Genesis LXE Regency Prolux Special Edition Prolux Plus Only Electrolux upright vacuums with the cord coming out of the very top of the handle are included in this recall. "Electrolux" and the model name are written on each vacuum.
Title: CPSC, Electrolux Announce Recall to Repair Top-Corded Vacuum Cleaners
ConsumerContact: For more information and to find the Electrolux store nearest to you, call Electrolux at (800) 896-9756 between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. EST Monday through Friday.

Products.Name: Ponytail Top-Corded Handle Upright Vacuum Cleaners

Images.Caption: Electrolux Ponytail Vacuum Cleaner

Injuries.Name: Electrolux is aware of at least 75 reports of the cords on these vacuums breaking or the casing around the cord exposing wires. About half of these incidents reportedly resulted in burns or shocks to users. Of these reports, there were 11 serious injuries which included consumers suffering second or third degree burns, shocks, or a combination of these injuries.

Retailers.Name: Most of these vacuums were sold through direct sales and retail stores, including Sam's Club, Service Merchandise and Macy's, between May 1991 and September 1993 for between $150 and $550, depending on the model and accessories. Some vacuums were sold directly to corporate customers.

Hazards.Name: The power cords on these vacuums extend out of the very top of the handle, and the cord is often used as an extension of the handle. The power cord can break inside the handle or the casing around the cord can break, and cause shocks or burns to the user's hand. Even when there is no apparent breaking of the casing around the cord, these vacuums can still cause injuries.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using these vacuums, and return them to an Electrolux store for a free repair. The handle on the vacuum will be replaced with a new model handle.

Description: The recalled grills are black and have a side burner for cooking, similar to a gas-range stove top. The model numbers of the grills are: 56GR8, 560R8, 562D1, 562D9, GC548517, GG546517, GS544417, GS544717, GS546517, GG546537 and GG547517. The complete model numbers can be found on the identification label on the back of the grill, and on the assembly instructions and parts list. The word, "GRILLMASTER" is written on the front of these grills. In March 1998, Sunbeam Products recalled grills with model numbers GG 461 EPB, GG 560 EPB, HG 560 EPB and GG 560 EPBS because of a similar hose placement hazard.
Title: CPSC and Sunbeam Products Inc. Announce Recall of Gas Grills With Side Burners
ConsumerContact: Consumers may call Sunbeam toll-free at (800) 200-2300 7:00 am to 5:00 pm, Monday through Friday.

Products.Name: Grillmaster gas grills with side burners

Images.Caption: Grillmaster gas grill with side burner
Grillmaster logo

Injuries.Name: Sunbeam Products received one complaint from a consumer who requested a replacement hose due to damage caused from the heat of the grill casting. There have been no reports of injuries associated with these grills.

Manufacturers.Name: Sunbeam Products Inc., of Neosho Mo.

Retailers.Name: Mass merchandise stores, such as Bradlees, Caldor, the Home Depot, Service Merchandise and Wal-Mart sold the grills nationwide, from 1996 through July 1998, for about $200 to $250.

Hazards.Name: The side burner's propane gas hose can twist up toward the aluminum casting of the grill, causing overheating and melting of the hose. Gas leakage or a fire could result from the hose damage.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the recalled grills immediately and call Sunbeam to receive a free retrofit kit. The retrofit kit contains a wire bracket guard and instructions for easy installation that will correctly position the side burner's propane gas hose.

Description: This recall involves charging stands with model number MMA008 and power banks with model numbers BPB002 and PB0003. Model number "MMA008" is printed on the bottom of the charging stand. Serial numbers (14 digits) starting with "57X" are included in this recall and are also printed on the bottom of the charging stand. Model number "BPB002" is printed on the back top of the power bank. Serial numbers (14 digits) starting with "35S" are included in this recall and are also printed on the back of the power bank. Model number "PB0003" is printed on the back of the power bank. All serial numbers are included in this recall. Both the charging stands and BPB002 power banks were sold in black. The PB0003 power banks were sold in black or white.
Title: Belkin Recalls Portable Power Banks and Wireless Charging Stands Due to Fire and Burn Hazards
ConsumerContact: Belkin toll-free at 800-223-5546 from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. ET Monday through Friday, online at http://www.belkin.com/MMA008recall and http://www.belkin.com/BPB002recall or at https://www.belkin.com/ and click on "Product Recalls" at the bottom of the page for more information.

Products.Name: Portable Power Banks and Wireless Charging Stands
Products.NumberOfUnits: About 83,500 (In addition, about 2,385 were sold in Canada)

Images.Caption: Recalled MMA008 Portable Wireless Charging Stand
Location of model number on the recalled MMA008 Portable Wireless Charging Stand (in red box)
Recalled BPB002 Portable Power Bank
Location of model number on the recalled BPB002 Portable Power Bank (in red box)
Recalled PB003 Portable Power Bank

Injuries.Name: The firm has received one report of a fire incident in the U.S. (and 15 reports internationally). Two minor burn injuries and property damage totaling $37,765 have been reported outside of the U.S.

Manufacturers.Name: Belkin International Inc., of El Segundo, California

Retailers.Name: Best Buy, Target, Walmart and other stores nationwide and online at Belkin.com, Amazon.com and on Tiktok from August 2020 through August 2025 for between $29 and $180.

Hazards.Name: The lithium-ion battery in the power banks and charging stands can overheat, posing fire and burn hazards to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled power banks and charging stands and contact Belkin to receive a full refund or store credit. Consumers should submit photos showing the front and back of the product with their recall submission form. Consumers can receive a full refund for the amount on the purchase receipt, if provided. If no receipt is provided, consumers can receive the average sales price for the model. Alternatively, consumers can choose to receive a Belkin store credit worth 20 percent more than the average sales price of the model. Note: Do not throw this recalled lithium-ion battery or device in the trash, the general recycling stream (e.g., street-level or curbside recycling bins), or used battery recycling boxes found at various retail and home improvement stores. Recalled lithium-ion batteries must be disposed of differently than other batteries, because they present a greater risk of fire. Your municipal household hazardous waste (HHW) collection center may accept this recalled lithium-ion battery or device for disposal. Before taking your battery or device to a HHW collection center, contact that office ahead of time and ask whether it accepts recalled lithium-ion batteries. If it does not, contact your municipality for further guidance.

Description: This recall involves Kimpex Rush and Kimpex Arrow II Ski Kits and Kimpex Rush and Kimpex Arrow II adaptor kits. The recalled kits are used to replace the skis on snowmobiles and were sold in red, green, yellow, white, black and blue. "Kimpex" is stamped on both sides of the snowmobile's ski handles.
Title: Kimpex Recalls Snowmobile Ski and Adaptor Kits Due to Crash Hazard and Risk of Serious Injury
ConsumerContact: Kimpex Inc. at 800-561-6461 from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. ET Monday through Friday, email at service@kimpex.com, or online at https://www.kimpex.com/en-us/page/safety-recalls or www.kimpex.com and click on "Safety Recalls" for more information. The firm is contacting all known purchasers directly.

Products.Name: Kimpex Ski and Adaptor Kits
Products.NumberOfUnits: About 1,980 (In addition, 2,600 were sold in Canada)

Images.Caption: Recalled Kimpex Rush ski kit and adaptor kit

Injuries.Name: The firm has received two reports of the skis falling off snowmobiles. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name: Kimpex USA dealers nationwide and online at Kimpex.com and other websites from April 2022 through January 2025 for between $300 and $500 for the Kimpex Rush and Kimpex Arrow II Ski Kits, and about $23 for the Ski Adaptor Kits.

Distributors.Name: Kimpex (U.S.A.) Ltd., of Champlain, New York

Hazards.Name: The skis can detach from the snowmobile, posing a crash hazard and risk of serious injury.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using snowmobiles equipped with the recalled Kimpex ski kits and adaptor kits, and contact a Kimpex dealer for a free repair kit.

Description: This recall involves Black Diamond Recon LT avalanche transceivers. The transceivers are plastic with an LCD screen. They have a gray exterior and a blue top. The Black Diamond logo and model name "RECON LT" are on the front of the transceivers. The recalled transceivers were sold as standalone units and as part of Black Diamond Alpine Avy Safety Sets and Black Diamond Recon LT Avy Safety Sets.
Title: Black Diamond Equipment Recalls BD Recon LT Avalanche Transceivers Due to Risk of Loss of Emergency Communications; Risk of Serious Injury or Death
ConsumerContact: Black Diamond toll-free at 866-306-0865 from 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. MT Monday through Friday, email at 2025reconltrecall@bdel.com, or online at https://www.blackdiamondequipment.com/en_US/content/product-recalls/ or www.blackdiamondequipment.com and click on "Product Recalls" located at the top of the webpage or for more information.

Products.Name: BD Recon LT Avalanche Transceivers
Products.NumberOfUnits: About 1,660 (In addition, about 206 were sold in Canada). The transceivers were recalled in 2023 for a different hazard

Images.Caption: Recalled Black Diamond Recon LT avalanche transceiver (front)
Recalled Black Diamond Recon LT avalanche transceiver (back)

Injuries.Name: The firm has received six reports of the switch mechanism malfunctioning due to corrosion. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name: Liberty Mountain, Recreational Equipment Inc. (REI) and other specialty outdoor stores nationwide and online at www.blackdiamondequipment.com, www.backcountry.com and www.evo.com from May 2021 through February 2025 for between $350 and $500.

Importers.Name: Black Diamond Equipment Ltd., of Salt Lake City, Utah

Hazards.Name: The metal contact in the switch mechanism of the Recon LT avalanche transceiver can corrode and cause the transceiver to malfunction. If this occurs, the device can turn off and make it impossible to locate a victim in an avalanche, which could result in serious injury or death.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled avalanche transceivers and contact Black Diamond for a full refund, a replacement transceiver, or a free repair. Consumers will not be asked for proof of purchase and will receive a pre-paid shipping label to return the recalled transceivers. Black Diamond is contacting all known purchasers. Consumers should go to https://warranty.bdel.com/beaconRecall2025/StepOne to participate in the recall. The repair involves replacing the original zinc coated steel insert with a corrosion resistant stainless-steel version. The replacement option allows the consumer to exchange their BD Recon LT avalanche transceiver for a BD Guide BT or BD Recon X avalanche transceiver. Both the BD Guide BT and BD Recon X transceivers utilize a different switch design. Consumers also have the option to return their device for a full refund (credit card reimbursement).

Description: The recalled Power Wheels cars and trucks have been sold under nearly 100 model names. The Power Wheels logo and the model name are on each vehicle. All models with two batteries are recalled, and certain models with one battery are recalled. The company will help consumers identify if their model is part of the recall. Power Wheels cars and trucks are intended for children 2 to 7 years old, and the vehicles' speed ranges from 1 to 5 mph, depending on the model. Power Wheels sold after October 1998 are not involved in this recall.
Title: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall to Repair Power Wheels Ride-On Battery-Powered Vehicles
ConsumerContact: Contact Fisher-Price online at www.service.mattel.com and click on "Recalls & Safety Alerts" or at 800-348-0751 from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. ET Monday through Friday for more information.

Products.Name: Fisher-Price Power Wheels

Images.Caption: Yellow Power Wheels Car
Red Power Wheels Jeep

Injuries.Name: CPSC and Fisher-Price have received approximately 700 reports of electrical components failing and overheating while the cars and trucks were being ridden, charged, parked or stored. About 150 fires have been reported. Nine children suffered minor burns to the hands, legs, or feet; and up to $300,000 in property damage to 22 houses and garages have been reported. There have also been 71 reports of vehicles not stopping. Six children suffered bruises, scratches or bumps when their vehicles hit a car, truck, pole, window or fence.

Retailers.Name: Toy and mass merchandise stores nationwide sold the cars and trucks since 1984 for about $70 to $300.

Hazards.Name: The vehicles' electrical components can overheat and cause fires. Children can suffer injuries from fires and house fires can occur. Additionally, wiring problems can prevent the vehicles from stopping.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should remove the vehicles' batteries right away and not let children use these Power Wheels vehicles. The firm will be providing pro-rated refunds based on the age of the recalled products.

Description: This recall involves CIYTI Light-Up Princess Costumes. The costumes include a blue dress with a crown and wand that light up, and a remote control. The crowns, scepters, and remote controls contain button batteries. There are no markings on the product. The package has “CIYTI’ on the front.
Title: FoShanShiNanHaiQuNuoAiTongZhuangShangHang Recalls CIYTI Light-Up Princess Costumes Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Battery Ingestion; Violate Mandatory Standard for Toys
ConsumerContact: Email at Norakid2026@outlook.com

Products.Name: CIYTI Light-Up Princess Costumes

Images.Caption: Recalled Light Up Princess Costume and Accessories
Recalled Princess Costume Dress

Injuries.Name: None reported

Retailers.Name:
Sold Online At:
Amazon from February 2025 through June 2025 for between $21 and $35.
FoShanShiNanHaiQuNuoAiTongZhuangShangHang, of China

Hazards.Name: The costumes violate the mandatory safety standard for toys because the button cell batteries can be accessed easily by children, posing a deadly ingestion hazard. If button cell or coin batteries are swallowed, the ingested batteries can cause serious injuries, including internal chemical burns, and death.

Remedies.Name:
Consumers should take the princess costumes away from children immediately, stop using them and contact FoShanShiNanHaiQuNuoAiTongZhuangShangHang for a full refund. Consumers will be asked to write “RECALLED” with permanent marker on the dress, crown, wand, and remote, then throw away the toys and submit a photo of the disposed toys to Norakid2026@outlook.com.  

Note: Button cell batteries are hazardous. Batteries should be disposed of or recycled by following local hazardous waste procedures.

Description: This recall involves Papablic bedside sleepers, model PAPA03001AI. These convertible sleepers function as both a bassinet and a play yard and have a gray exterior with an interior printed in a stars‑and‑moon pattern. The products have "Papablic" stitched in white on the front gray fabric panel. Model "PAPA03001AI" is printed on a label sewn to the interior fabric of the bassinet underneath the mattress pad.
Title: Papablic, of USA Recalls Convertible Bedside Sleepers Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Entrapment, Suffocation and Fall Hazards; Violate Mandatory Standard for Play Yards
ConsumerContact: Papablic by email at support@papablic.com, or online at https://papablic.com/pages/black-and-gray-bassinet-with-play-yard-extension-recall or https://papablic.com and click on "Recall Information" at the bottom of the page.

Products.Name: Papablic Bedside Sleepers with Play Yard Extensions

Images.Caption: Recalled Papablic Convertible Bedside Sleeper
Recalled Papablic Convertible Bedside Sleeper in Play Yard Mode

Injuries.Name: None reported.

Retailers.Name:
Sold Online At:
Amazon.com and papablic.com from April 2025 through July 2026 for about $190.

Distributors.Name: Papablic, Inc., doing business as Papablic, of USA, of Chicago, Illinois

Hazards.Name: The bedside sleepers with play yard extensions violate the mandatory safety standard for play yards because the mattress can become displaced, causing a baby to become entrapped between the sleeping pad and bottom posing a deadly suffocation hazard. In addition, the latching and locking mechanism can fail, causing the product to collapse, posing a risk of serious injury or deadly entrapment and fall hazards.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the convertible bedside sleeper immediately and contact Papablic for a refund. Consumers will be asked to disassemble the product, cut the mattress and fabric components in half and email photos of the destroyed components to support@papablic.com. Upon receipt of proof of destruction, Papablic will issue a full refund and consumers should dispose of the product.

Description: The screwdrivers were sold under the DeWalt, GRABBER, and Black & Decker Industry & Construction brand names. The DeWalt, model numbers are DW251, DW252, DW257, DW260K, DW265, DW266, DW267, DW268, DW268G, DW269, DW272, DW274, DW274-220, DW274W, DW275QD (Quik Drive ), DW276, DW281, DW282 and DW284. The GRABBER model numbers are 4060 and 4063. The Black & Decker Industry & Construction model numbers are 2121, 2125 and 2141. Only numeric date codes from 9601 to 9833 are included in this recall. The date code is followed by various letters. Those date codes ending with an "R" have already been repaired. The model number and date code are located on the nameplate, which is on the right hand side of the screwdriver when viewed from the back. The DeWalt and Quik Drive corded screwdrivers have a yellow housing with black accents. The GRABBER models have a black housing. The Black & Decker Industry & Construction models have a charcoal-gray housing.
Title: CPSC, DeWalt Industrial Tool Co. Announce Recall to Repair Electric Screwdrivers
ConsumerContact: To find the nearest service center or for more information, consumers should call DeWalt toll-free at (800) 433-9258 between 8 a.m and 4:30 p.m. EST Monday through Friday.

Products.Name: DeWalt corded electric screwdrivers

Injuries.Name: DeWalt has received reports of 40 of these screwdrivers causing shocks during use. There have been three reports of injuries resulting from these shocks.

Manufacturers.Name: DeWalt Industrial Tool Co., of Hampstead, Md.

Retailers.Name: Major chain home centers and hardware stores, as well as local hardware stores, nationwide sold these screwdrivers, from November 1996 through September 1998, for about $69 to $169, depending on the model.

Hazards.Name: The screwdrivers' wiring design can result in the user being shocked.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these screwdrivers immediately and take them to the nearest DeWalt/Black & Decker service center for a free repair.

Description: The NIKE Air Face Up men's basketball shoes being recalled are model numbers 830080, 139358 and 630327. The model number is located on the label on the inside tongue of the shoe, above the UPC code. The shoe is a mid-cut men's basketball shoe that comes in multiple color combinations. The shoe has a visible window, about 2 inches long, in the heel of the shoe. The words "NIKE AIR" are on the outside tongue of the shoe. The word "TEAM" is on the back of the shoe.
Title: CPSC, NIKE Announce Recall of Men's "Air Face Up" Basketball Shoes
ConsumerContact: For more information about the recall, consumers should call NIKE at (800) 344-6453 between 7:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. PST Monday through Friday.

Products.Name: NIKE Air Face Up men's basketball shoes

Images.Caption: Recalled NIKE Air Face Up men's basketball shoes

Injuries.Name: NIKE has received about 35 reports of high school and college age basketball players receiving cuts to the lower legs, including two reports of players requiring stitches.

Manufacturers.Name: NIKE USA Inc., of Beaverton, Ore.

Retailers.Name: Major athletic shoe stores and department stores nationwide sold the NIKE Air Face Up basketball shoes, from June 1998 through October 1998, for about $85.

Hazards.Name: The basketball shoes have a small decorative metal rivet located on the outside of the shoe, that can bend and form a sharp edge.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these basketball shoes and should immediately return them to the store where purchased, to receive a substitute product or a store credit.

Description: The vampire capes are made of black vinyl. The edges of the cape are scalloped. The capes are packaged in a plastic sleeve with a cardboard insert, which reads in part, "Child's Vinyl Vampire Cape...No. 50282...Made in China." The Rubie's logo and a picture of a boy wearing the cape are also on the insert. The witch brooms are 27 inches long with a bamboo handle and brush made of twigs. The brooms were sold with a sticker around the handle, which reads in part, "Child's Authentic Witch Broom...Style No. 85." The Rubie's logo is also on the sticker.
Title: CPSC, Rubie's Costume Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Vampire Capes and Witch Brooms
ConsumerContact: For questions about this recall, consumers should call Rubie's Costume Co. Inc. collect at (516) 488-0484 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. EST Monday through Friday.

Products.Name: Children's vampire capes and witch brooms

Manufacturers.Name: Rubie's Costume Co. Inc., of Richmond Hill, N.Y.

Retailers.Name: Toy, party, costume, discount and drug stores nationwide sold the capes and brooms for about $2 each, from September 1997 to October 1998.

Hazards.Name: The capes and the brooms, which fail to meet federal mandatory standards for flammability, could ignite readily and present a serious risk of burn injuries to children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should not let their children wear the vampire capes or use the 27-inch witch brooms this Halloween. Consumers should return the products to the stores where purchased, for a refund.

Description: This recall involves Luminaires with certain adjustable tilt mounting arms manufactured between August 2019 to July 2020 and August 2024 to April 2026: AASP, AARP, AAWB, and AAWSC. The adjustable tilt arm mounts the RSX luminaire to a square pole, round pole, wall bracket or wall bracket with surface mount conduit. The arm mount allows the luminaire to be tilted from 0 degrees to 90 degrees above horizontal. Consumers should contact Lithonia Lighting to confirm their Luminaire with adjustable tilt mounting arms are included in the recall.
Title: Lithonia Lighting Recalls RSX Luminaires with Adjustable Tilt Arm Mountings Due to Risk of Serious Injury from Impact Hazard
ConsumerContact: Lithonia Lighting toll-free at 855-307-2454 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday, online at  https://lithonia.acuitybrands.com/ and click on “Recalls” at the bottom of the page for more information.

Injuries.Name: The firm has received 13 reports of adjustable tilt arm mountings breaking. There have been four reports of the fixtures falling. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name:
Sold At:
Commercial distributors nationwide including Turtle & Hughes Inc. and Consolidated Electrical Distributors for commercial outdoor lighting applications from August 2019 to August 2026 for between $400 and $2200.

Hazards.Name: The knuckle of the recalled adjustable tilt arm mountings can fail, allowing the luminaire to fall from the mounting arm, posing a risk of serious injury due to impact hazard.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should keep clear of the area directly beneath the Luminaire and contact Lithonia Lighting to schedule a free repair. Lithonia Lighting will arrange for a qualified professional to replace the recalled adjustable tilt arm mount with a new complete adjustable arm assembly.

Description: This recall involves VQQQ-branded natural gas patio heaters, models VQQQ-A1 and VQQQ-001. Description: This recall involves the Scotch™ thermal laminator, model number TL1302Z.  The laminator is light gray/white with gray accents and the word "Scotch" is printed in gray on the front. The laminating slot is approximately 13 inches wide, and the machine has a carrying handle on the right side of the machine when viewing from the front. The model number TL1302Z is located on the sticker on the bottom of the laminator and can also be found on the product packaging.
Title: 3M Company Recalls Scotch™ Thermal Laminators Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Fire Hazard
ConsumerContact: 3M Company toll-free at 800-772-4337 from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. CT Monday through Friday, online at https://www.scotchbrand.com/3M/en_US/scotch-brand/tl1302Z-laminator-recall/ or www.scotchbrand.com and click on "Recall Information" at the top of the page for more information.

Products.Name: Scotch™ Thermal Laminators

Recalled Scotch™ Thermal Laminator package

Injuries.Name: The firm has received 63 reports of the laminators smoking, melting and overheating, including five reports of the laminators catching fire and one report of minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name:
Sold Online At:
Amazon.com from June 2024 through September 2026 for between $44 and $56.

Hazards.Name: The recalled thermal laminators can overheat, posing a fire hazard.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using and unplug the recalled thermal laminators immediately and contact 3M Company to receive a full refund. The refund, in the form of a check, will be mailed to the consumer upon receipt of the completed form and confirmation that the laminator's power cord has been cut. Consumers should dispose of the recalled laminator in accordance with local and state laws governing electronics recycling.

Description: This recall involves all units of the Hatsan Blitz and Blitz 777 pellet shooting air rifles sold from February 2020 through March 2026. Both the Blitz and Blitz 777 pellet air rifles were sold in .22, .25 and .30 calibers. The pellet air rifles are gas operated and select-fire (semi-auto/full-auto) pre-charged pneumatic (PCP). They are black and feature a synthetic stock, a carbon fiber air tank mounted beneath the barrel and a rotary magazine feed. Serial numbers and manufacturing dates are engraved on the right side of the receiver above the bolt. On the left side of the receiver is the Hatsan logo, featuring a circular mark, with the word "HATSAN" next to a graphic of a bow and arrow. The model name "BLITZ" or "BLITZ 777" is also marked on the left side of the receiver.
Title: HatsanUSA Recalls Blitz Air Rifles Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Projectile Hazard
ConsumerContact: HatsanUSA toll-free at 877-750-3375 from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. CT Monday through Friday, email at blitzrecall@hatsanusa.com or online at https://hatsanairgunsusa.com/recalls/blitz-and-blitz-777-recall/ and enter password "Hatsan2026!" or https://hatsanairgunsusa.com and click "Warranty & Safety" and then "Recalls" for more information.

Some models have support legs and motion-sensor lights. The recalled bed rails have "KingPavonini" written on the fabric cover. Description: This recall involves VEVOR Garment Steamers used to remove wrinkles from clothing and textiles. The recalled steamer has an oval-shaped opening for the steam vents and the steamer body is white with "VEVOR" and "TOUGH TOOLS, HALF PRICE" printed in orange lettering on the side of the product beneath the water reservoir window. There is a red toggle power switch on the handle. "VEVOR," "Garment Steamer," "FCL-H09," and "Manufacturer: Guangdong ESINO Technology Group Co., Ltd" are printed on a label on the bottom of the product. The recalled steamer was sold with a silver-colored glove.
Title: Sanven Technology Recalls VEVOR Steamers Due to Risk of Serious Injury from Burn Hazard
ConsumerContact: Sanven Technology toll-free at 855-599-6320 from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. PT Monday through Friday, email at recalling@vevor.com, or online at vevor.com/pages/vevor-steamer-recall or at www.vevor.com and click on "Product Recall" at the top of the page for more information.

Injuries.Name: The Firm has received six reports of hot water spitting, pouring out, leaking or dripping from the steamers, and 12 reports of issues with the water tank cap detaching, leaking, not staying closed, fitting loosely, or melting. The reported cap issues resulted in two burn injuries, including one consumer who received a permanent scar and a second-degree burn from the hot water, after the steamer's cap suddenly detached and one consumer who received a minor burn on their hand and fingers from leaked water. Additionally, there is one report of a minor steam burn through the provided glove.

Retailers.Name: Online at Vevor.com, Amazon.com and HomeDepot.com from December 2023 to September 2025 for between about $10 and $33.

Distributors.Name: Sanven Technology Ltd., dba VEVOR, of Rancho Cucamonga, California

Hazards.Name: The steamers can leak or spit hot water, posing a risk of serious burn injury to users and bystanders. The water tank cap can also leak or detach during use, exposing users to hot water.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled steamers and contact Sanven Technology for a full refund. Consumers will be asked to provide their contact information and send a photo of the steamer with its unplugged cut power cord to receive a full refund.
